STATUS as of 2026-08-04 (see state-adoption-plan.md §9.9-§9.12): Phase A2 is COMPLETE — all 10 import_unchanged addresses (3 security groups, ALB, 2 listeners, 4 security-group rules) have been imported into the live backend (environments/staging/ecs/terraform.tfstate). This correction (Phase A3 adoption alignment) reviewed and re-verified, read-only, all 12 addresses not already covered by the four now-imported security-group rules, landed several code fixes (ECS launch-mode/desired-count modeling, cluster capacity-provider representability, IAM inline-policy name alignment), corrected stale prior-audit claims (capacity-provider association, assign_public_ip "hard stop" framing), and recorded a still-open elasticache:ListTagsForResource permission gap. See each entry's notes field for its Group A/B/C readiness classification. No Terraform apply is authorized by any of this — nothing here approves an actual import, ECS deployment, scaling change, capacity-provider association, IAM permission migration, or description-drift reconciliation.

counting_methodology.explanation: Terraform's resource count is variable-dependent (count/for_each conditionals). This manifest counts the resource graph that results when every REQUIRED (no-default) variable is set to the value needed to describe this specific live environment, and every OPTIONAL (has-a-default) variable is left at its current repository default. This is the only way to produce a single deterministic total; a different tfvars file could produce a different count.
required_vars_assumed_set_to_live_values: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids (live default VPC and its subnets)
rds_security_group_id (sg-0d4c5eedb2ee21743, enables the 2 count-gated postgres SG rules)
redis_auth_token (required, no default, sourced from Secrets Manager - enables the replication group)
ses_events_queue_arn, ses_events_queue_url, ses_events_dlq_arn (enables ses_consumer's SQS IAM policy and the 3 SQS-based alarm resources)
ses_sending_identity_arn, ses_authorized_from_address (enables the web task role's SES-send policy)
alarm_sns_topic_arn (has no default; required for the cloudwatch_alarms module to be usable at all)
optional_vars_left_at_repository_default: enable_custom_metric_alarms = false (repository default; app-level custom-metric emission does not exist yet) - excludes 4 alarm resource addresses (queue_depth_high, oldest_queued_job_age_high, failed_jobs_high, scheduler_heartbeat_missing) from the total entirely, since their count expression evaluates to 0

resources.prerequisite: CORRECTED 2026-08-05: two separate issues, both now fixed. (1) elasticache:ListTagsForResource is now GRANTED for firmsbase-staging-operator on this resource's ARN (confirmed via a direct read-only aws elasticache list-tags-for-resource call on 2026-08-05) — the prior permission gap is resolved. (2) A second, previously undiscovered issue: this module's aws_elasticache_subnet_group resource derived its subnet_ids unconditionally from the caller's ECS private_subnet_ids (only 2 subnets), but the live subnet group actually registers 6 subnets across every AZ in the VPC (confirmed via aws elasticache describe-cache-subnet-groups and aws ec2 describe-subnets — all 6 exist, belong to vpc-0fd81b688155ded2b, are in "available" state, in AZs us-east-1a through 1f). Conflating ECS task placement with ElastiCache subnet-group membership meant this resource address could never have represented live's actual membership. FIXED: modules/elasticache now takes a required subnet_ids input (no default, decoupled from private_subnet_ids); the staging root's new elasticache_subnet_ids variable (null default, falling back to private_subnet_ids for a brand-new environment) is set to the exact live 6-subnet set in this environment's terraform.tfvars. Importing will record the current, correct 6-subnet membership only; it does NOT authorize removing any subnet later — any future reduction or redesign requires a separate, explicit availability, failover, networking, and maintenance review. The resource address (module.elasticache.aws_elasticache_subnet_group.this) is unchanged. This subnet group remains unimported until this correction merges; the replication group remains a later, separate import.

This is a real, unreviewed Terraform-managed setting mismatch: importing under the old hardcoded config would have left the next (unauthorized) plan proposing to enable Container Insights on a live, in-use cluster — a real cost/behavior change, not a no-op. The module renders "disabled" for this environment; the normal new-environment default remains "enabled" (var.ecs_container_insights_enabled defaults true at the staging root). Importing the cluster records the current disabled setting; it does NOT authorize enabling Container Insights later — that requires a separate, explicit cost and observability review. The resource address (module.ecs_cluster.aws_ecs_cluster.this) is unchanged. No exact, source-backed blocker remains — this address is now genuinely suitable for an individual Phase A3 canary import. The separate empty capacity-provider association (module.ecs_cluster.aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_providers.this) remains a different Terraform resource address and a later, independent import — not part of this correction or this import.

resources.prerequisite: CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (§9.17): the name-alignment fix (var.iam_task_execution_role_name) already landed; this pass fixes the remaining role-level gaps found by a fresh field-by-field live comparison. (1) Trust policy — live's assume-role policy for BOTH firmsbase-staging-ecs-execution-role and firmsbase-staging-ecs-task-role carries identical StringEquals aws:SourceAccount=603013471426 / ArnLike aws:SourceArn=arn:aws:ecs:us-east-1:603013471426:* conditions (re-confirmed via aws iam get-role on both roles, 2026-08-05); modules/iam's shared ecs_tasks_assume_role data source previously had no conditions at all. Fixed: the shared document now takes required aws_account_id/aws_region inputs and renders both conditions for every role that uses it (task_execution and all 7 task roles), matching live exactly — not modeled as a role-specific document, since both examined live roles are identical. (2) Description — live is "Execution role for FirmsBase staging ECS tasks"; the module previously declared no description argument at all. Fixed: a new required task_execution_role_description module input (wired ONLY to aws_iam_role.task_execution.description) is set to the exact live value in terraform.tfvars. Neither fix touches aws_iam_role_policy.task_execution, the AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy attachment, or any permission grant — the inline-policy content/permission-shape decision (§11 item 3) remains entirely separate and unresolved. With both the trust policy and description now matching live exactly, the role-level configuration is complete; this address is suitable for an isolated role-only import after this correction merges. Importing the role does not authorize detaching AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy or replacing the inline policy's content — either is a separate, explicitly reviewed decision. iam:ListRoleTags is AccessDenied for this operator, but is likely NOT a real import-time blocker: IAM's GetRole embeds Role.Tags inline (confirmed: this role currently has zero tags, consistent with an omitted Tags field), so the AWS provider's aws_iam_role Read typically does not need a separate tags call. Not claimed as a required permission without a real import proving otherwise.

Confirmed live content: Version 2012-10-17, one statement (Sid AllowOnlyFirmsVaultStagingSender), Effect Allow, Action [ses:SendEmail, ses:SendRawEmail], Resource “*” (wildcard), Condition StringEquals ses:FromAddress=no-reply@staging-mail.firmsvault.com. The shared role has zero attached managed policies — this inline statement is its entire live permission set. This proposed policy intentionally narrows that grant three ways: (1) drops the unused ses:SendEmail action — confirmed by direct code inspection that Illuminate\Mail\Transport\SesTransport only ever calls ses:SendRawEmail; (2) scopes Resource from wildcard to the exact verified identity ARN (arn:aws:ses:us-east-1:603013471426:identity/staging-mail.firmsvault.com) — SES SendEmail/SendRawEmail support identity-ARN resource scoping, so this is a genuine least-privilege narrowing, not something the wildcard was ever required for; (3) moves the grant off the shared role (technically reachable by worker/critical-worker/scheduler even though none of them call SES) onto web only. The FromAddress condition value is preserved exactly (no-reply@staging-mail.firmsvault.com matches live byte-for-byte). The audit found no unexplained permission difference — every narrowing traces to a cited, verified reason.
